image:
  repository: forge.ko.ag/sauyon/lemonade
  # Bump on each rebuild. CI tags as :sha-<short> alongside :latest;
  # pinning to a sha keeps ArgoCD diffs explicit.
  tag: "sha-e785204"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # No pullSecrets: package visibility follows the owner, and `sauyon` is a
  # public user, so the kubelet pulls this anonymously.

replicas: 1

# Models that the init wrapper registers + loads at first start. The /v1/pull
# calls are idempotent against the PVC's user_models.json, so restarts skip
# downloads. Backend options are pinned via /v1/load with save_options=true,
# persisting to ~/.cache/lemonade/recipe_options.json.
models:
  # `user.*` namespace required by Lemonade for HF-registered models.
  #
  # huihui-ai abliterated build of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (refusal-direction
  # removed via Arditi et al.). Quant tag is repo-native plain Q4_K — this
  # repo ships Q2_K..Q8_0 with no _M/_S split. Despite the "MTP-GGUF" repo
  # name, the only extra file is mmproj-model-f16.gguf (VLM projector);
  # there is no MTP draft file like ggml-org/* ships, so the resolver
  # won't accidentally pick a draft GGUF as the main model.
  #
  # Name is ALL-LOWERCASE on purpose. Lemonade matches model ids
  # case-sensitively, but Cloudflare AI Gateway lowercases the model field
  # before forwarding to a custom provider. A mixed-case name therefore
  # 404s (→ 502) for every request that arrives via ai.ko.ag/CF AIG, while
  # working fine on direct in-cluster calls. Keeping the registered id
  # lowercase makes CF's normalization a no-op. See docs/lemonade-cf-aig-model-casing.md.
  - name: "user.qwen3.6-35b-abliterated"
    checkpoint: "huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-abliterated-MTP-GGUF:Q4_K"
    # Vulkan wins on Strix Halo across the board in our bench; ROCm
    # variance was poor on MoE long-context (+/-11 t/s on 17.95).
    backend: "vulkan"
    # Total context across all slots -- llama.cpp's `--ctx-size` is total, not
    # per-slot. llama-server then caps each slot at the model's training
    # context, 262144 here, logging "the slot context (N) exceeds the training
    # context of the model". So the only ctxSize worth setting is
    # parallelSlots * 262144; anything above that is allocated and wasted, and
    # anything below shortens every slot for no gain.
    #
    # Four slots because every observed failure was a fan-out of 3+ concurrent
    # requests queueing against 2 slots until the client gave up. Costs ~4Gi of
    # the 96Gi Vulkan/GTT budget over two slots (24.5Gi -> 28.6Gi measured);
    # GTT is charged to host DRAM but never to this pod's cgroup, so the memory
    # limit below does not move. See docs/lemonade-prompt-cache.md.
    ctxSize: 1048576
    parallelSlots: 4
    # KV cache quant. Q4_0 halves Q8_0 again, which is required to fit
    # long-context slots under the pod limit. If Vulkan fails to load with
    # a cache type support error, fall back to q8_0 and drop slots.
    kvCacheType: "q4_0"
    # Required for non-f16 KV quant to actually save memory at runtime.
    flashAttention: true
    # Overrides the template baked into the GGUF, which rejects any system
    # message that is not first. Clients that send two — opencode does, once
    # a memory plugin is loaded — get a 400 on every request without this.
    # Names a file under files/. See docs/lemonade-chat-template.md.
    chatTemplateFile: "qwen3.6-sysmerge.jinja"
    # llama-server's `--cache-ram`: the RAM ceiling for saved prompt state,
    # which is what lets a conversation resume without re-evaluating its whole
    # prompt. Default 8192 evicted 3 times in 48h. This cgroup has swap
    # disabled, so every MiB here is permanently resident.
    cacheRamMiB: 16384
    # llama-server's `--ctx-checkpoints`. Each checkpoint is a flat 62.8 MiB,
    # so the default 32 lets one long conversation hold ~2 GiB of the cache
    # above. Restores here land on the newest checkpoint, so the deep history
    # bought nothing. See docs/lemonade-prompt-cache.md.
    ctxCheckpoints: 8

# Sole registered model, so this is also what clients that do not pass a
# model explicitly get.
defaultModel: "user.qwen3.6-35b-abliterated"

# Make `models:` above authoritative: on every start, drop registry entries
# on the PVC that aren't listed there. Without this, registrations are
# add-only and survive forever — a model removed from this file keeps
# showing up in /api/tags, which is how the mixed-case Qwen orphan outlived
# the rename. Set false if you want to register models by hand through
# lemond's web UI and have them stick across restarts.
#
# Prunes registrations only, never GGUF blobs — see the entrypoint comment
# in templates/configmap.yaml for why that split is deliberate.
pruneUnmanagedModels: true

# Lemonade caches HF downloads + recipe_options.json under /root/.cache.
# 100 GiB is oversized now that Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K (~21 GiB) is the only
# model — kept as-is because Longhorn cannot shrink a bound PVC in place.

persistence:
  storageClass: longhorn
  size: 100Gi

# Vulkan reads /dev/dri/renderD128; /dev/kfd is unused but harmless.
# Capacity advertised as 1 on Strix Halo — only one GPU-requesting pod
# can be scheduled at a time, which is fine now that ollama is retired.

  enabled: true
  resourceName: amd.com/gpu

# A/B-only escape hatch — set `enabled: true` if you ever need to run
# this Pod alongside another holder of amd.com/gpu. Bypasses the
# capacity gate by hostPath-mounting the render node directly; pod
# pinned to the GPU host via nodeSelector (no device plugin to tell
# the scheduler where the hardware lives). Compute time-slices.

  enabled: false
  renderNode: /dev/dri/renderD128
  nodeSelector:
